properties.text: Come, Indra, and delight thee with the juice at all the Soma feasts, Protector, mighty in thy strength.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: To Indra pour ye forth the juice, the active gladdening juice, to him The gladdening omnific God.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: O Lord of all men, fair of cheek, rejoice thee in the gladdening buds, Present at these drink-offerings.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Songs have outpoured themselves to thee, Indra, the strong, the guardian Lord. And raised themselves unsatisfied.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Send to us bounty manifold, O Indra, worthy of our wish, For power supreme is only thine.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: O Indra, stimulate thereto us emulously fain for wealth. And glorious, O most splendid One.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Give, Indra, wide and lofty fame, wealthy in cattle and in strength, Lasting our life-time, failing not.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Grant us high fame, O Indra, grant riches bestowing thousands, those Fair fruits of earth borne home in wains.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Praising with songs the praise-worthy who cometh to our aid, we call Indra, the Treasure-Lord of wealth.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: To lofty Indra, dweller by each libation, the pious man Sings forth aloud a strengthening hymn.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: In all libations men with hero spirit urge thee, Universal, One, each seeking several light, each fain to win the light apart. Thee, furthering like a ship, will we set to the chariot pole of strength, As men who win with sacrifices Indra's thought, men who win Indra with their lauds.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Couples desirous of thine aid are storming thee, pouring their presents forth to win a stall of kine, pouring gifts, Indra, seeking thee. When two men seeking spoil or heaven thou bringest face to face in war, Thou showest Indra, then the bolt thy constant friend, the bull that ever waits on thee,
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Also this morn may he be well inclined to us, mark at our call our offerings and our song of praise, our call that we may win the light. As thou, O Indra Thunder-armed, wilt, as the Strong One, slay the foe, Listen, thou to the prayer of me a later sage, hear thou a later sage's prayer.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: All these libations are for thee, O Hero: to thee I offer these my prayers that strengthen. Ever, in every place, must men invoke thee.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Never do men attain, O Wonder-worker, thy greatness, Mighty One who must be lauded, Nor, Indra, thine heroic power and bounty.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Bring to the Wise, the Great who waxeth mighty your offerings and make ready your devotion: To many clans he goeth, man's Controller.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: When, with the Princes, Maghavan, famed of old, comes nigh the thunderbolt of gold and the Controller's car Which his two tawny coursers draw, then Indra is the Sovran Lord of power whose fame spreads far and wide.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: With him too is this rain of his that comes like herds: Indra throws drops of moisture on his yellow beard. When the sweet juice is shed he seeks the pleasant place, and stirs the worshipper as the wind disturbs the wood.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: We laud and praise his several deeds of valour who, fatherlike,. with power hath made us stronger; Who with his voice slew many thousand wicked ones who spake in varied manner with contemptuous cries.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: O Soma-drinker, ever true, utterly hopeless though we be, Do thou, O Indra, give us hope of beauteous horses and of kine, In thousands, O most wealthy One.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: O Lord of strength, whose jaws are strong, great deeds are thine, the powerful: Do thou, O Indra, give us hope of beauteous horses and of kine, In thousands, O most wealthy One.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Lull thou asleep, to wake no more, the pair who on each other look: Do thou, O Indra, give us hope of beauteous horses and of kine, In thousands, O most wealthy One.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Hero, let hostile spirits sleep, and every gentler Genius wake: Do thou, O Indra, give us hope of beauteous horses and of kine, In thousands, O most wealthy One.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Destroy this ass, O Indra, who in tones discordant brays to thee: Do thou, O Indra, give us hope of beauteous horses and of kine, In thousands, O most wealthy One.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Far distant on the forest fall the tempest in a circling course; Do thou, O Indra, give us hope of beauteous horses and of kine, In thousands, O most wealthy One.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Slay each reviler and destroy him who in secret injures us: Do thou, O Indra, give us thope of beauteous horses and of kine, In thousands, O most wealthy One.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Couples desirous of thine aid are storming thee, pouring their presents forth to win a stall of king pouring gifts, Indra, seeking thee. When two men seeking spoil or heaven thou bringest face to face in war, Thou showest, Indra, then the bolt, thy constant friend, the bull that ever waits on thee.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: This thine heroic power full well the people knew, wherewith thou brakest down, Indra, autumnal forts, brakest them down with conquering might. Thou hast chastised. O Indra, Lord of strength, the man who worships not, And made thine own this great earth and these water-floods, with joyous heart these water-floods.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: And they have bruited far this hero might, when thou, O Strong One, in thy joy helpest thy suppliants who sought to win thee for their Friend. Their battle-cry thou madest sound victorious in the shocks of war. One stream after another have they gained from thee, eager for glory have they gained.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: As sits the young bird on the tree rejoicing, ye, swift pair, have been roused by clear laudation, Whose Hoter-priest through many days is Indra, earth's guardian, friend of men, the best of heroes.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: May we, when this Dawn and the next dance hither, be thy best servants, most heroic Hero! Let the victorious car with triple splendour bring hitherward the hundred chiefs with Kutsa.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: What was the gladdening draught that pleased thee, Indra? Speed to our doors, our songs, for thou art mighty. Why comest thou to me, what gift attracts thee? Fain would I bring thee food most meet to offer.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Indra, what fame hath one like thee mid heroes? With what plan wilt thou act? Why hast thou sought us? As a true friend, Wide-Strider! to sustain us, since food absorbs the thought of each among us.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Speed happily those, as Sūrya ends his journey, who meet his wish as bridegrooms meet their spouses; Men who support, O Indra strong by nature, with food the many songs that tell thy praises.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Thine are two measures, Indra, wide, well-meted, heaven for thy majesty, earth for thy wisdom. Here for thy choice are Somas mixed with butter: may the sweet meath be pleasant for thy drinking.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: They have poured out a bowl to him, to Indra, full of sweet juice, for faithful is his bounty. O'er earth's expanse hath he grown great by wisdom, the friend of man, and by heroic exploits.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Indra hath conquered in his wars the mighty: men strive in multitudes to win his friendship. Ascend thy chariot as it were in battle, which thou shalt drive to us with gracious favour,
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Impetuous, true, let Maghavan come hither, and let his tawny coursers speed to reach us. For him have we pressed juice exceeding potent: here, praised with song, let him effect his visit.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Unyoke, as at thy journey's end, O Hero, to gladden thee to-day at this libation. Like Usanā, the priest a laud shall utter, a hymn to thee, the Lord Divine, who markest.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: When the Bull quaffing praises our libation, as a sage paying holy rites in secret, Seven singers here from heaven hath he begotten, who e'en by day have wrought their works while singing.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: When heaven's fair light by hymns was made apparent. (they made great splendour shine at break of morning), He with his succour, best of heroes, scattered the blinding dark- ness so that men saw clearly.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Indra, impetuous One, hath waxed immensely: he with his vastness hath filled earth and heaven. E'en beyond this his majesty extendeth who hath exceeded all the worlds in greatness,
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Sakra who knoweth well all human actions hath with his eager friends let loose the waters. They with their songs cleft e'en the mountain open, and willingly disclosed the stall of cattle.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: He smote away the flood's obstructer Vritra: Earth conscious lent her aid to speed thy thunder. Thou sentest forth the waters of the ocean as Lord through power and might, O daring Hero.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: When, Much-invoked! the waters' rock thou deftest, Saramā showed herself and went before thee. Hymned by Angirases, bursting the cowstalls, thou foundest ample strength for us as leader.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Sing this, what time the juice is pressed, to him your Hero much-invoked, To please him as a mighty, Bull.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: He, excellent, withholdeth not his gift of power and wealth in kine, When he hath listened to our songs.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: May he with might disclose for us the cows' stall, whosesoe'er it be, To which the Dasyu-slayer goes.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: O Indra, give us wisdom as a sire gives wisdom to his sons. Guide us, O Much-invoked, on this our foray: may we, living, still enjoy the light.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Grant that no mighty foes, unknown, malevolent, unhallowed, tread us to the ground. With thine assistance, Hero! may we pass through all the waters that are rushing down.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Bring us, O Indra, name and fame, enriching, mightiest, excellent, Wherewith, O wondrous God, fair-cheeked and thunder-armed, thou hast filled full this earth and heaven.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: We call on thee, O King, mighty among the Gods, ruler of men, to succour us, All that is weak in us, excellent God, make firm: make our foes easy to subdue.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: O Indra, if a hundred heavens and if a hundred earths were: thine No, not a hundred suns could match thee at thy birth, not, both, the worlds, O Thunderer.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Thou, Hero, hast performed thy hero needs with might, yea, all+ with strength, O Strongest One. Maghavan, help us to a stable full of kine, O Thunderer, with) wondrous aids.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: If I, O Indra, were the lord of riches ample as thine own, I should support the singer, God who scatterest wealth! and! not abandon him to woe.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Each day would I enrich the man who sang my praise, in what- soever place he were. No kinship is there better, Maghavan, than thine: a father even) is no more.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: O Indra, grant a happy home, a triple refuge, triply strong. Bestow a dwelling-place on the rich lords and me, and keep thy dart afar from these.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: They who with minds intent on spoil subdue the foe, boldly attack and smite him down. From these, O Indra, Bounteous Lord who lovest song, be closest guardian of our lives.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: O Indra marvellously bright, come, these libations long for thee, Thus by fine fingers purified.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Urged by the holy singer, sped by song, come, Indra, to the prayers. Of the libation-pouring priest.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Approach, O Indra, hasting thee, Lord of Bay Horses, to the prayers: Take pleasure in the juice we pour.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Glorify naught besides, O friends; so shall no sorrow trouble you. Praise only mighty Indra when the juice is shed, and say your lauds repeatedly:
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Even him, eternal, like a bull who rushes down, men's con- queror, bounteous like a cow; Him who is cause of both, of enmity and peace, to both sides most munificent.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Although these men in sundry ways invoke thee to obtain thine aid. Be this our prayer, addressed, O Indra, unto thee, thine exalta- tion every day.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Those skilled in song, O Maghavan, among these men o'ercome with might the foeman's songs, Come hither, bring us strength in many a varied form most near that it may succour us.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Those who are yoked by prayer with prayer I harness, the two. fleet friendly Bays who joy together. Mounting thy firm and easy car, O Indra, wise and all-knowing come thou to the Soma.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Priests, offer to the Lord of all the people the milked-out stalk of Soma, radiant-coloured. No wild bull knows his drinking-place like Indra who ever seeks him who hath pressed the Soma.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Thou dost desire to drink, each day that passes, the pleasant food which thou hast had aforetime. O Indra, gratified in heart and spirit, drink eagerly the Soma set before thee.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Thou, newly-born, for strength didst drink the Soma; thy mother told thee of thy future greatness. O Indra, thou hast filled mid-air's wide region, and given the Gods by battle room and freedom.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: When thou hast urged the arrogant to combat, proud in their strength of arm, we will subdue them. Or, Indra, when thou fightest girt by heroes, we in the glorious fray with thee will conquer.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: I will declare the earliest deeds of Indra, and recent acts which Maghavan hath accomplished. When he had conquered godless wiles and magic, Soma became his own entire possession.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Thine is this world of flocks and herds around thee, which with the eye of Surya thou beholdest. Thou, Indra, art alone the Lord of cattle: may we enjoy the treasure which thou givest.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Ye twain are Lords of wealth in earth and heaven, thou, O Brihaspati, and thou, O Indra . Mean though he be, give wealth to him who lauds you. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Him who with might hath propped earth's ends, who sitteth in threefold seat, Brihaspati, with thunder, Him of the pleasant tongue have ancient sages, deep thinking,. holy singers, set before them.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Wild in their course, in well-marked wise rejoicing were they,. Brihaspati, who pressed around us Preserve, Brihaspati, the stall uninjured,r,this company's raining. ever-moving birth-place.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Brihaspati, from thy remotest distance have they sat down who love the law eternal. For thee were dug wells springing from the mountain, which murmuring round about pour streams of sweetness.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Brihaspati, when first he had his being from mighty splendour in supremest heaven. Strong, with his sevenfold mouth, with noise of thunder, with his seven rays blew and dispersed the darkness.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: With the loud-shouting band who sang his praises, with thunder, he destroyed malignant Vala. Brihaspati thundering drave forth the cattle, the lowing cows who make oblations ready.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Serve we with sacrifices, gifts, and homage even thus the Steer of all the Gods, the Father. Brihaspati, may we be lords of riches, with noble progeny and, store of heroes.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Even as an archer shoots afar his arrow, offer the laud to him with meet adornment. Quell with your voice the wicked's voice, O sages, Singer, make Indra rest beside the Soma.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Draw thy Friend to thee like a cow at milking: O singer, wake up Indra as a lover. Make thou the Hero haste to give us riches even as a vessel filled brimful with treasure.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Why, Maghavan, do they call thee bounteous Giver? Quicken me: thou, I hear, art he who quickens. Sakra, let my intelligence be active, and bring us luck that finds great wealth, O Indra.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Standing, in battle for their rights, together, the people, Indra, in the fray invoke thee. Him who brings gifts the Hero makes his comrade: with him who pours no juice he seeks not friendship.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Whoso with plenteous juice for him expresses strong Somas as much quickly-coming treasure, For him he everthrows in early morning his swift well-weapon- ed foes and slays the tyrant.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: He unto whom we offer praises, Indra, Maghavan, who hath joined to ours his wishes Before him even afar the foe must tremble: low before him must bow all human glories.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: With thy fierce bolt, O God invoked of many, drive to a distance from afar the foeman. O Indra, give us wealth in corn and cattle, and make the singer's prayer gain strength and riches.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Indra the swallower of strong libations with their thick residue, the potent Somas, He, Maghavan, will not restrict his bounty: he brings much wealth unto the Soma-presser.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Yea, by superior play he wins advantage when he, a gambler, piles his gains in season. Celestial-natured, he o'erwhelms with riches the devotee who keeps not back his money.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: O much-invoked, may we subdue all famine and evil want with store of grain and cattle. May we allied, as first in rank, with princes,:obtain possessions by our own exertion
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Brihaspati protect us from the rearward, and from above and from below, from sinners. May Indra from the front and from the centre, as friend to friends, vouchsafe us room and freedom.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Served with oblations, first-born, mountain-render, Angiras' Son, Brihaspati the holy. With twice-firm path, dwelling in light, our Father, roars loudly, as a bull, to earth and heaven.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Brihaspati who made for such a people wide room and verge when Gods were invocated— Slaying his foe he breaketh down their cattles, quelling his enemies and those who hate him.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Brihaspati in war hath won rich treasures, hath won, this God, the great stalls filled with cattle. Striving to win waters and light, resistless, Brihaspati with light- ning smites the foeman.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: This holy hymn sublime and seven-headed, sprung from eternal Law, our sire discovered. Ayāsya, friend of all men, hath engendered the fourth hymn as he sang his laud to Indra.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Thinking aright, praising eternal Order, the sons of Dyaus the Asura, those heroes, Angirases, holding the rank of sages, first honoured sacrifice's holy statute.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Girt by his friends who cried with swanlike voices, bursting the stoney barriers of the prison, Brihaspati spake in thunder to the cattle, and uttered praise and. song when he had found them.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Apart from one, away from two above him, he draye the kine that stood in bonds of falsehood. Brihaspati, seeking light amid the darkness, draye forth the bright cows: three he made apparent.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: When he had cleft the lairs and western castle, he cut off three from him who held the waters. Brihaspati discovered, while he thundered like Dyaus, the dawn,. the sun, the cow, the lightning.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: As with a hand, so with his roaring Indra cleft Vala through,. the guardian of the cattle. Seeking the milk-draught with sweat-shining comrades he stole: the Pani's kine and left him weeping.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: He with bright faithful friends, winners of booty, hath rent the milker of the cows asunder. Brihaspati with wild boars strong and mighty sweating with heat hath gained a rich possession.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: They, longing for the kine, with faithful spirit incited with their hymns the Lord of cattle. Brihaspati freed the radiant cows with comrades self-yoked,. averting shame from one another.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: In our assembly with auspicious praises exalting him who roareth. like a lion. May we in every fight where heroes conquer rejoice in strong. Brihaspati the victor.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: When he had won him strength of every nature and gone to heaven and its most lofty mansions, Men praised Brihaspati the mighty, bringing the light within their mouths from sundry places.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Fulfil the prayer that begs for vital vigor: aid in your wonted manner e'en the humble. Let all our foes be turned and driven backward. Hear this, O Heaven and Earth, ye all-producers.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Indra with mighty strength hath cleft asunder the head of Arbuda the watery monster, Slain Ahi, and set free the Seven Rivers. O Heaven and Earth, with all the Gods, protect us.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Praise, even as he is known, with song Indra the guardian of the kine, The Son of Truth, Lord of the brave.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Hither his bay steeds have been sent, red steeds are on the sacred grass. Where we in concert sing our songs.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: For Indra thunder-armed the kine have yielded mingled milk and meath. What time he found them in the vault.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: When I and Indra amount on high up to the bright One's place and home, We, having drunk of meath, will reach his seat whose Friends are three-times-seven.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Sing, sing ye forth your songs of praise, ye Priyamedhas, sing your songs: Yea, let young children sing their lauds: as a strong castle praise ye him.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Now loudly let the viol sound, the lute send out its voice with might, Shrill be the music of the string. To Indra is the hymn upraised.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: When hither speed the dappled cows, unflinching, easy to be milked, Seize quickly, as it bursts away, the Soma juice for Indra's drink.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Indra hath drunk; Agni hath drunk all Deities have drunk their fill. Here Varuna shall have his home, to whom the floods have sung aloud as mother-kine unto their calves.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Thou, Varuna, to whom belong the Seven Streams, art a glorious God. The waters flow into thy throat as'twere a pipe with ample mouth.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: He who hath made the fleet steeds spring, well-harnessed, to the worshipper, He, the swift guide, is that fair form thot loosed the horses near at hand.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Indra, the very mighty, holds his enemies in utter scorn. He, far away, and yet a child, cleft the cloud smitten by his voice.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: He, yet a boy exceeding small, mounted his newly-fashioned car. He for his Mother and his Sire cooked the wild mighty buffalo.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Lord of the Home, with beauteous cheeks, ascend thy chariot wrought of gold. We will attend the heavenly One; the thousand-footed, red of hue, matchless, who blesses where he goes.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: With reverence they come hitherward to him as to a sovran lord, That they may bring him near for this man's good success, to prosper and bestow his gifts.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: The Priyamedhas have observed the offering of the men of old, Of ancient custom, while they strewed the sacred grass and spread their sacrificial food.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: He who as sovran Lord of men moves with his chariots unrestrained, The Vritra-slayer, queller of all fighting hosts, preeminent, is praised in song.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Honour that Indra, Puruhanman! for his aid, in whose sustain- ing hand of old. The splendid bolt of thunder was deposited, as the great Sun was set in heaven.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: No one by deed attains to him who works and strengthens evermore: No, not by sacrifice, to Indra praised of all, resistless, daring, bold in might;
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: The potent Conqueror, invincible in war, him at whose birth the mighty ones, The kine who spread afar, sent their loud voices out, heavens, earths sent their loud voices out.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: O Indra, if a hundred heavens and if a hundred earths were thine No, not a thousand suns could match thee at thy birth, not both the worlds, O Thunderer.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Thou, Hero, hast performed thy hero deeds with might, yea, all with strength, O Strongest One. Maghavan, help us to a stable full of kine, O Thunderer, with wondrous aids.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: May our hymns give thee great delight. Display thy bounty, Thunderer. Drive off the enemies of prayer.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Crush with thy foot the niggard churls who bring no gifts. Might art thou: There is not one to equal thee.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Thou art the Lord of Soma pressed, Soma unpressed is also thine, Thou art the Sovran of the folk.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Swaying about the active Ones came nigh to Indra at his birth, And shared his great heroic might.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Based upon strength and victory and power, O Indra is thy birth. Thou, Mighty One, art strong indeed.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Thou art the Vritra-slayer, thou, Indra, hast spread the firmament: Thou hast with might upheld the heavens.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Thou, Indra, bearest in thine arms the lightning that accords with thee, Whetting thy thunderbolt with might.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Thou, Indra, art pre-eminent over all creatures in thy strength: Thou hast pervaded every place.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: May Sovran Indra come to the carousal, he who by holy Law is strong and active. The overcomer of all conquering forces with his great bull-like power that hath no limit.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Firm-seated is thy car, thy steeds are docile: thy hand, O King, holds, firmly grasped, the thunder. On thy fair path, O Lord of men, come quickly: we will increase thy power when thou hast drunken.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Let strong and mighty steeds who bear this mighty Indra, the Lord of men, whose arm wields thunder, Bring unto us, as shares of our banquet, the Bull of conquering might, of real vigour.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: So like a bull thou rushest to the Lord who loves the trough, the Sage, the prop of vigour, in the vat. Prepare thine energies, collect them in thyself: be for our profit as the Master of the wise.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: May precious treasures come to us,— so will I pray. Come to the votary's gift offered with beauteous laud. Thou art the Lord, as such sit on this holy grass: thy vessels are inviolate as Law commands.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Far went our earliest invocations of the Gods, and won us glories that can never be surpassed. They who could not ascend the ship of sacrifice sink down in desolation, trembling with alarm.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: So be the others, evil-hearted, far away, whose horses difficult to harness have been yoked. Here in advance man stand anear to offer gifts, by whom full many a work that brings reward is done.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: He firmly fixed the plains and mountains as they shook. Dyaus thundered forth and made the air's mid-region quake. He stays apart the two confronting bowls; he sings lauds in the potent Soma's joy when he hath drunk.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: I bear this deftly-fashioned goad of thine wherewith thou, Maghavan, shalt break the strikers with the hoof. At the libation mayst thou be well satisfied. Partake the juice, partake the banquet, Bounteous Lord.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: O Much-invoked, may we subdue all famine and evil want with store of grain and cattle. May we allied, as first in rank, with princes, obtain possessions by our own exertions.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Brihaspati protect us from the rearward, and from above, and from below, from sinners! May Indra from the front and from the centre, as friend to friends, vouchsafe us room and freedom.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: From the three jars the Great and Strong hath drunk drink blent with meal. With Vishnu hath he quaffed the flowing Soma juice, all that he would. That hath so heightened him the Great, the Vast, to do his mighty work. So may the God attend the God, true Indu Indra who is true.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Sing strength to Indra that shall set his chariot in the foremost place. Giver of room in closest fight, slayer of foes in shock of war, be thou our great encourager. Let the weak bowstrings break upon the bows of feeble enemies.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Thou didst destroy the Dragon: thou sentest the rivers down to earth. Foeless, O Indra, wast thou born. Thou tendest well each choicest thing. Therefore we draw us close to thee. Let the weak bowstrings break upon the bows of feeble enemies.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Destroyed be all malignities and all our enemy's designs. Thy bolt thou castest at the foe, O Indra, who would smite us dead: thy liberal bounty gives us wealth. Let the weak bow- strings break upon the bows of feeble enemies.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Taste this strong draught that gives thee vital vigour: with all thy chariot here unyoke thy coursers. Let not those other sacrificers stay thee, Indra: these juices shed for thee are ready.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Thine is the juice effused, thine are the juices yet to be pressed: our resonant songs invite thee. O Indra, pleased to-day with this libation, come, thou who knowest all, and drink the Soma.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Whoso, devoted to the God, effuses Soma for him with yearning heart and spirit, Never doth Indra give away his cattle: for him he makes the lovely Soma famous.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: He looks with loving favour on the mortal who, like a rich man, pours for him the Soma. Maghavan in his bended arm supports him: he slays, unasked, the men who hate devotion.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: We call on thee to come to us, desirous of booty, and of cattle, and of horses. For thy new love and favour are we present: let us invoke thee, Indra, as our welfare.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: For life I set thee free by this oblation from the unknown decline and from consumption; Or, if the grasping demon have possessed him, free him from her, O Indra, thou and Agni.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Be his days ended, be he how departed, be he brought very near to death already, Out of Destruction's lap again I bring him, save him for life to last a hundred autumns.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: With thousand-eyed oblation, hundred-autumned, bringing a hundred lives, have 1 restored him. That Indra for a hundred years may lead him safe to the farther shore of all misfortune.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Live waxing in thy strength a hundred autumns, live through a hundred springs, a hundred winters. Through hundred-lived oblation Indra, Agni, Brihaspati, Savitar yield him for a hundred!
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: So have I found and rescued thee: thou hast returned with youth renewed. Whole in thy members! I have found whole sight and all thy life for thee.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: May Agni yielding to our prayer, the Rakshas-killer, drive away. The malady of evil name that hath beset thy labouring womb.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Agni, concurring in the prayer, drive off the eater of thy flesh, The malady of evil name that hath attacked thy babe and womb.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: That which destroys the sinking germ, the settled, moving embryo, That which would kill the babe at birth, even this will we drive far away.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: That which divides thy legs that it may lie between the married pair, That penetrates and licks thy side, even this will we exterminate.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: What rests by thee in borrowed form of brother, lover, or of lord, And would destroyed the progeny,—even this will we exter- minate.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: That which through sleep or darkness hath deceived thee and lies down by thee, And will destroy thy progeny,—even this will we exterminate.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: From both thy nostrils, from thine eyes, from both thine ears and from thy chin, Forth from thy head and brain and tongue I drive thy malady away.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: From the neck-tendons and the neck, from the breast-bones and from the spine, From shoulders, upper, lower arms, I drive thy malady away.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: From viscera and all within, forth from the rectum, from the heart, From kidneys, liver and from spleen, I drive thy malady away.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: From thighs, from knee-caps, and from heels, and from the forepart of the feet, From hips, from stomach, and from groin, I drive thy malady away.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: From what is voided from within, and from thy hair, and from thy nails, From all thyself, from top to toe, I drive thy malady away.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: From every member, every hair, disease that comes in every joint, From all thyself, from top to toe, I drive thy malady away.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Avaunt, thou Master of the Mind, I Depart and vanish far away. Look on Destruction far from us. The live man's mind is manifold.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Here verily yesterday we let the Thunder-wielder drink his fill. So in like manner, offer him the juice to day. Now range you. by the Glorious One.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Even the wolf, the savage beast that rends the sheep, follows the path of his decrees. So, India, graciously accepting this our praise, with wondrous. thought come forth to us.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: What manly deed of vigour now remains that Indra hath not done? Who hath not heard his glorious title and his fame, the Vritra- slayer from his birth?
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: That we may win us wealth and spoil we poets verily call on thee. In war men call on thee, Indra, the hero's Lord, in the steed's, race-course call on thee.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: As such, O Wonderful whose hand holds thunder, praised as mighty, Caster of the Stone. Pour on us boldly, Indra, kie and chariot-steeds, ever to be the conqueror's strength.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Men with their lauds are urging thee, Indra, to drink the Soma first. The Ribhus in accord have lifted up their voice and Rudras. sung thee as the First.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Indra increased his manly strength at sacrifice, in the wild rapture of this juice; And living men to-day, even as of old, sing forth their praises to his majesty.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Now have we, Indra, Friend of Song, sent our great wishes forth to thee. Coming like floods that follow floods.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: As rivers swell the ocean, so, Hero, our prayers increase thy might, Though of thyself, O Thunderer, waxing day by day.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: With holy song they bind to the broad wide-yoked car the bay steeds of the rapid God, Bearers of India, yoked by prayer.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Agni we choose, the messenger, the herald, master of all wealth,. Well skilled in this our sacrifice.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: With calls they ever invocate Agni, Agni, Lord of the House, Oblation-bearer, much-beloved.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Bring the Gods hither, Agni, born for him who strews the sacred grass. Thou art our herald, meet for praise.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Meet to be lauded and adored, showing in beauty through the= dark, Agni the Bull is kindled well,
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Agni is kindled as a Bull, like a horse bearer of the Gods; Men with oblations worship him.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Thee will we kindle as a Bull, we who are bulls ourselves, O Bull, Thee, Agni, shining mightily.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Solicit with your hymns, for aid, Agni the God with piercing flame, For riches famous Agni, Purmilha ‘and ye men, Agni to light our dwelling well.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Agni, come hither with thy fires: we choose thee as our Hotai- priest. Let the extended ladle full of oil balm thee, best priest, to sit on sacred grass.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: For unto thee, O Angiras, O Son of Strength, move ladles in the sacrifice, To Agni, Child of Force, whose locks drop oil, we seek, fore- most in sacrificial rites.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: May these my songs of praise exalt thee, Lord who hast abun- dant wealth. Men skilled in holy hymns, bright with the hues of fire, have sung them with their lauds to thee.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: He with his might enhanced by Rishis thousand-fold, hath like an ocean spread himself. His majesty is praised as true at solemn rites, his power where holy singers rule
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: May Indra, who in every fight must be invoked, be near to us. May the most mighty Vritra-slayer, meet for praise, come to libations and to hymns.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Thou art the best of all in sending bounteous gifts, true art thou,. lordly in thine act. We claim alliance with the very Glorious One, yea, with the- mighty Son of Strength.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Thou in the battles, Indra, art subduer of all hostile bands. Father art thou, all-conquering, cancelling the curse, thou victor of the vanquisher.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: The earth, and heaven cling close to thy victorious might, as sire and mother to their child. When thou attackest Vritra all the hostile bands shrink and faint, Indra at thy wrath.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Bring to your aid the Eternal One, who shoots and none may shoot at him, Inciter, swift, victorious, best of charioteers, Tugrya's unvan- quished strengthener;
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: HE who, as Sovran Lord of men, moves with his chariots unrestrained, The Vrtra-slayer vanquisher, of fighting hosts, preeminent, is praised with song.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda, 2nd ed.

properties.text: Honour that Indra, Puruhanman! for his aid, in whose sustaining hand of old, The splendid bolt of thunder was deposited, as the great Sun was set in heaven.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda, 2nd ed.

Griffith's attributed Rigveda translation of that verse is therefore a published translation of exactly this text. Both keys: VG:AV:SAU:K20:S105:V005 and VG:RV:SAK:M08:S070:V002.
