properties.text: That lofty energy of thine, thy strength and thine intelligence, Thy thunderbolt for which we long, our wish makes keen.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: O Indra, heaven and earth augment thy manly power and thy renown, The waters and the mountains stir and urge thee on.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Vishnu, the lofty Ruling Power, Varuna, Mitra sing thy praise: In thee the Maruts' company hath great delight.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Before his hot displeasure all the peoples, all the men bow down, As rivers bend them to the sea.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: This power of his shone brightly forth when Indra brought to- gether like A skin the worlds of earth and heaven.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: The fiercely-moving Vritra's head he severed with his thunder- bolt, His hundred-knotted thunderbolt.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: In all the worlds That was the best and highest whence sprang the mighty God, of splendid valour. As soon as born he overcomes his foemen, he in whom all who lend him aid are joyful.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Grown mighty in his strength, with ample vigour, he as a foe strikes fear into the Dāsa, Eager to win the breathing and the breathless. All sang thy praise at banquet and oblation.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: All concentrate on thee their mental vigour, what time these, twice or thrice, are thine assistants. Blend what is sweeter than the sweet with sweetness: win quickly with our meath that meath in battle.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Therefore in thee too, thou who winnest riches, at every banquet are the sages joyful With mighter power, bold God, extend thy firmness: let not malignant Yātudhānas harm thee.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Proudly we put our trust in thee in battles, when we behold great wealth the prize of combat. I with my words impel thy weapons onward, and sharpen with my prayer thy vital vigour.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Worthy of praises many-shaped, most skilful, most energetic, Āptya of the Aptyas: He with his might destroys the seven Dānus, subduing many who were deemed his equals.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Thou in that house which thy protection guardedh bestowest- wealth, the higher and the lower. Thou stablishest the two much-wandering Mothers, and bringest many deeds to their completion.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Brihaddiva, the foremost of light-winners, repeasts these holy prayers, this strength to Indra. He rules the great self-luminous fold of cattle, and all the doors of light hath he thrown open.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Thou hath Brihaddiva the great Atharvan, spoken to Indra as himself in person. The Mātarisvarīs, the spotless sisters, with power exalt him and impel him onward.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Bright, Presence of the Gods, the luminous herald, Siirya hath mounted the celestial regions. Day's maker, he hath shone away the darkness, and radiant passed o'er places hard to traverse.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: The brilliant Presence of the Gods hath risen, the eye of Mitra, Varuna, and Agni. The soul of all that moveth not or moveth, Sūrya hath filled the earth and air and heaven.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Even as a lover followeth a maiden, so doth the Sun the Dawn, refulgent Goddess: Where pious men extend their generations before the Gracious One for happy fortune.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: O Indra, bring great strength to us, bring valour, Satakratu, thou most active, bring. A hero conquering in war.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: For, gracious Satakratu, thou hast ever been a mother and a sire to us, So now for bliss we pray to thee.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: To thee, Strong, Much-invoked who showest forth thy strength, O Satakratu, do I speak: So grant thou us heroic might.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: The juice of Soma thus diffused, sweet to the taste, the bright Cows drink Who for the sake of splendour close to mighty Indra's side rejoice, good in their own supremacy.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Craving his touch the dappled Kine mingle the Soma with their milk. The milch-kine dear to Indra send forth his death-dealing thun- derbolt, good in their own supremacy.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: With veneration, passing wise, honouring his victorious might, They follow close his many laws to win them due preeminence, good in their own supremacy.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: For Indra, lover of carouse, loud be our songs about the juice: Let poets sing the hymn of praise.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: We summon Indra to the draught, in whom all glories rest, in whom The seven communities rejoice.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: By the three Soma jars the Gods span sacrifice that stirs the mind: Let our songs aid and prosper it.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: If, Indra, thou drink Soma by Vishnu's or Trita Āptya's side, Or with the Maruts take delight in flowing drops;
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Or, Sakra, if thou gladden thee afar or in the sea of air, Rejoice thee in this juice of ours, in flowing drops.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Or, Lord of Heroes, if thou aid the worshipper who sheds the juice, Or him whose laud delights thee, and his flowing drops.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Whatever, Vritra-slayer! thou Sūrya, hast risen upon to-day, That, Indra, all is in thy power.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: When, Mighty One, Lord of the Brave, thou thinkest, I shall never die, That thought of thine is true indeed.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Thou, Indra, goest unto all Soma libations shed for thee, Both far away and near at hand.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Both boons—may Indra hitherward turned, listen to this, prayer of ours, And, mightiest Maghavan with thought inclined to us come nigh to drink the Soma juice.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: For him, strong independent Ruler, Heaven and Earth have fashioned forth for power and might. Thou seatest thee as first among thy peers in place, for thy soul longs for Soma juice.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: O Indra, from all ancient time rivalless ever and companionless art thou: In war thou seekest comradeship.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Thou findest not the wealthy man to be thy friend: those scorn thee who are flown with wine. What time thou thunderest and gatherest, then thou, even as a father, art invoked.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: I from my Father have received deep knowledge of the holy Law: I was born like unto the Sun.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: After the lore of ancient time I make, like Kanva, beauteous songs, And Indra's self gains strength thereby.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Whatever Rishis have not praised thee, Indra, or have lauded thee, By me exalted wax thou strong.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Never may we be cast aside and strangers, as it were to thee. We, Thunder-wielding Indra, count ourselves as trees rejected and unfit to burn.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: O Vritra slayer, we were thought slow and unready for the fray: Yet once in thy great bounty may we have delight, O Hero, after praising thee.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Drink Soma, Lord of Bays, and let it cheer thee: Indra, the stone, like a well-guided courser, Directed by the presser's arms hath pressed it.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: So let the draught of joy, thy dear companion, by which, O Lord of Bays, thou slayest foemen, Delight thee, Indra, Lord of princely treasures.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Mark closely, Maghavan; the words I utter, this eulogy recited by Vasishtha: Accept the prayers I offer at thy banquet.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Indra with all thy saving helps give us assistance, Lord of Power For after thee we follow even as glorious bliss, thee, Hero, finder-out of wealth.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Increaser of our steeds and multiplying kine, a golden well, O God, art thou; For no one may impair the gifts laid up in thee, Bring me what- ever thing I ask.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Indra for worship of the Gods, Indra while sacrifice proceeds, Indra as warriors in the battle-shock we call, Indra that we may win the spoil.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: With might hath Indra spread out heaven and earth, with power hath Indra lighted up the Sun. In Indra are all creatures closely held; in him meet the distilling Soma drops.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: An ancient praise-song hath been sung: to Indra have ye said the prayer. They have sung many a Brihatī of sacrifice, poured forth th, worshipper's many thoughts.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: In zealous haste the singers have sung forth a song distilling oil and rich in sweets. Riches have spread among us, and heroic strength; with us are flowing Soma drops.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Though, Indra, thou art called by men eastward and westward, north and south, Thou chiefly art with Anava and Turvasa, brave Champion! urged by men to come.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Or, Indra, when with Ruma, Rusama, Syāvaka, and Kripa thou rejoicest thee, Still do the Kanvas bring praises, with their prayers, O Indra, draw thee hither: come.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Over the three great distances, past the Five Peoples go thy way, O Indra, noticing our voice.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Send forth thy ray like Sūrya: let my songs attract thee hither- ward. Like waters gathering to the vale.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: With Indra splendid feasts be ours enriched with ample spoil, wherewith, Wealthy in food, we may rejoice.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Like thee, thyself, the singers' friend, thou movest as it were, besought, Bold One, the axle of the car.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: That, Satakratu, thou to grace and please thy praisers, as it were, Stirrest the axle with thy strength.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: This is the Godhead, this the might of Sūrya: he hath with- drawn what spread o'er work unfinished. When he hath loosed his horses from their station, straight over all night spreadeth out her garment.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: In the sky's lap the Sun this form assumeth for Mitra and for Vāruna to look on. His bay steeds well maintain his power eternal, at one time bright and darksome at another.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: With what help will he come to us, wonderful, ever-waxing Friend, With what most mighty company?
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: What genuine and most liberal draught will spirit thee with juice to burst. Open e'en strongly-guarded wealth?
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Do thou who art protector us thy friends who praise thee With hundred aids approach us.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: We will, with Indra and all Gods to help us, bring these existing worlds into subjection. Our sacrifice, our bodies, and our offspring shall Indra form together with the Ādityas.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: With the Ādityas, with the band of Maruts, may Indra be pro- tector of our bodies. As when the Gods came after they had slaughtered the Asuras, keeping safe their Godlike nature,
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Brought the Sun hitherward with mighty powers, and looked about them on their vigorous Godhead. With this may we obtain strength God-appointed, and joy with brave sons through a hundred winters.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Drive all our enemies away, O Indra, the western, mighty Con- queror, and the eastern, Hero, drive off our northern foes and southern, that we in thy wide shelter may be joyful.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: What then? As men whose fields are full of barley reap the ripe corn removing it in order, So bring the food of those men, bring it hither, who come not to prepare the grass for worship.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Men come not with one horse at sacred seasons; thus they obtain no honour in assemblies. Sages desiring herds of kine and horses strengthen the mighty Indra for his friendship.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Ye, Asvins, Lords of Splendour, drank full draughts of grateful Soma juice, And aided Indra in his work with Namuchi of Asura birth.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: As parents aid a son, both Asvins, Indra, aided thee with their wondrous powers and wisdom When thou, with might, hadst drunk the draught that glad- dens, Sarasvati, O Maghavan refreshed thee.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Indra is strong to save, rich in assistance: may he, possessing all, be kind and gracious. May he disperse our foes and give us safety, and may we be the lords of hero vigour.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: May we enjoy his favour, his the holy: may we enjoy his blessed loving-kindness. May this rich Indra, as our good protector, drive off and keep afar all those who hate us.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Men have abstained from pouring juice; nor counted Indra as a God. Where at the votary's store my friend Vrishākapi hath drunk his fill. Supreme is Indra over all.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Thou, Indra, heedless passest by the ill Vrishākapi hath wrought; Yet nowhere else thou findest place wherein to drink the Soma juice. Supreme is Indra over all.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: What hath he done to injure thee, this tawny beast Vrishākapi, With whom thou art so angry now? What is the votary's food- ful store? Supreme is Indra over all.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Soon may the hound who hunts the boar seize him and bite him in the ear, O Indra, that Vrishākapi whom thou protectest as a friend. Supreme is Indra over all.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Kapi hath marred the beauteous things, all deftly wrought, that were my joy. In pieces will I rend his head; the sinner's portion shall be woe. Supreme is Indra over all.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: No dame hath ampler charms than I, or greater wealth of love's delights. None with more ardour offers all her beauty to her lord's embrace. Supreme is Indra over all.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Mother whose love is quickly won,I say what verily will be, My breast, O mother, and my head and both my hips seem quivering Supreme is Indra over all.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Dame with the lovely hands and arms, with broad hair-plaits and ample hips, Why, O thou hero's wife, art thou angry with our Vrishākapi? Supreme is Indra over all.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: This noxious creature looks on me as one bereft of hero's love. Yet heroes for my sons have I, the Maruts' friend and Indra's Queen Supreme is Indra over all.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: From olden time the matron goes to feast and general sacrifice. Mother of heroes, Indra's Queen, the rite's ordainer is extolled. Supreme is Indra over all.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: So have I heard Indrāni called most fortunate among these dames, For never shall her Consort die in future time through length of days. Supreme is Indra over all.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Never, Indrāni have I joyed without my friend Vrishākapi, Whose welcome offering here, made pure with water, goeth to the Gods. Supreme is Indra over all.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Wealthy Vrishākapāyi, blest with sons and consorts of thy sons, Indra will eat thy bulls, thy dear oblation that effecteth much. Supreme is Indra over all.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Fifteen in number, then, for me a score of bullocks they prepare. And I devour the fat thereof: they fill my belly full with food. Supreme is Indra over all.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Like as a bull with pointed horn, loud bellowing amid the herds, Sweet to thine heart, O Indra, is the brew which she who tends thee pours. Supreme is Indra over all.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Indrāni speaks. Non ille fortis (ad Venerem) est cujus mentula laxe inter femora dependet; fortis vero estille cujus, quum sederit, membrum pilosum se extendit. Super omnia est Indra.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96
properties.language_correction: staged as 'en'; the literal is Griffith's Latin substitution, verified against the pinned source page

properties.text: Indra speaks. Non fortis est ille cujus, quum sederit, membrum pilosum se extendit: fortis vero est ille cujus mentula laxe inter femora dependet. Super omnia est Indra.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96
properties.language_correction: staged as 'en'; the literal is Griffith's Latin substitution, verified against the pinned source page

properties.text: O Indra, this Vrishākapi hath found a slain wild animal, Dresser, and new-made pan, and knife, and wagon with a load of wood. Supreme is Indra over all.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Distinguishing the Dāsa and the Arya, viewing all, I go. I look upon the wise, and drink the simple votary's Soma juice. Supreme is Indra over all.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: The desert plains and steep descents, how many leagues in length they spread! Go to the nearest houses, go unto thine home, Vrishākapi. Supreme is Indra over all.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Turn thee again Vrishākapi; we twain will bring thee happiness. Thou goest homeward on thy way along this path which leads to sleep. Supreme is Indra over all.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: When, Indra and Vrishākapi, ye travelled upward to your home, Where was that noisome beast, to whom went it, the beast that troubles man? Supreme is Indra over all.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Daughter of Manu, Parsu bare a score of children at a birth. Her portion verily was bliss although her burthen caused her grief.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Listen to this, ye men, a laud of glorious bounty shall be sung. Thousands sixty, and ninety we, O Kaurama, among the Rusamas have received.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Camels twice-ten that draw the car, with females by their side, he gave. Fain would the chariot's top bow down escaping from the stroke of heaven.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: A hundred chains of gold, ten wreaths, upon thee Rishi he bestowed, And thrice-a-hundred mettled steeds, ten-times-a-thousand cows he gave.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Glut thee, O Singer, glut thee like a bird on a ripe-fruited tree. Thy lips and tongue move swiftly like the sharp blades of a pair of shears.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Quickly and willingly like kine forth come the singers and their hymns: Their little maidens are at home, at home they wait upon the cows.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: O Singer, bring thou forth the hymn that findeth cattle, findeth: wealth. Even as an archer aims his shaft address this prayer unto the Gods.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: List to Parikshit's eulogy, the sovran whom all people love, The King who ruleth over all, excelling mortals as a God.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: 'Mounting his throne, Parikshit, best of all, hath given us peace and rest,' Saith a Kauravya to his wife as he is ordering his house.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: 'Which shall I set before thee, curds, gruel of milk, or barley- brew?' Thus the wife asks her husband in the realm which King Parikshit rules.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Up as it were to heavenly light springs the ripe corn above the cleft. Happily thrive the people in the land where King Parikshit reigns.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Indra hath waked the bard and said, Rise, wander singing here and there. Praise me, the strong: each pious man will give thee riches in return,
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Here, cows! increase and multiply, here ye, O horses, here, O men. Here, with a thousand rich rewards, doth Pūshan also seat him- self.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: O Indra, let these cows be safe, their master free from injury. Let not the hostile-hearted or the robber have control of them.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Oft and again we glorify the hero with our hymn of praise, with prayer, with our auspicious prayer. Take pleasure in the songs we sing: let evil never fall on us.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: The worshipper who pours the juice, for gathering and assembly fit, And yonder foe-destroying Sun,—these have the Gods designed of old.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: He who defiles a sister, he who willingly would harm a friend, The fool who slights his elder, these, they say, must suffer down. below.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Whenever any good man's son becometh bold and spirited, Then hath the wise Gandharva said this pleasant upward-point- ing word.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: The most unprofitable churl, the wealthy men who brings no. gift, These, verily, as we have heard, are cast away by all the wise.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: But they who have adored the Gods, and they who have best- owed their gifts, Those liberal lords are filled with wealth like Sūrya risen up to heaven.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: With unanointed eyes and limbs, wearing no gem or ring of gold. No priest, no Brāhman's son is he: these things are ordered in the rules.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: With well-anointed limbs and eyes, wearing fair gem and golden, ring, Good priest is he, the Brāhman's son; these things are ordered in the rules.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Pools with no place for drinking, and the wealthy man who. giveth naught, The pretty girl you may not touch, these things are ordered in: the rules.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Pools with good drinking places, and the wealthy man who freely gives, The pretty girl who may be touched, these things are ordered in the rules.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: The favourite wife neglected, and the man who safely shuns the fight, A sluggish horse whom none may guide, these things are order- ed in the rules.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: The favourite wife most dearly loved, the man who safely goes to war, The fleet steed who obeys the rein, these things are ordered in the rules.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: When, Indra, thou, as no man could, didst plunge into the Ten Kings' fight, That was a guard for every man: for he is formed to stay disease.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Easily conquering Maghavan, thou, Hero, bentest Raji down, Rentest asunder Rauhina, calvest in pieces Vritra's head.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Thou who didst separate the clouds and penetrate the water- floods, To thee, great slayer of the foe, be glory, Indra, yea, to thee!
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: They said to Auchchaihsravasa running as side-horse of the Bays, Safely to victory, O Steed, bear Indra with the beauteous wreath.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: They yoke the white mares, on the Bay's right harness Auchchai- hsravasa. He joyeth as he carrieth Indra the foremost of the Gods.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: These mares come springing forward to Pratipa Prātisutvana.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: One of them is Hariknikā. Hariknikā, what seekest thou?
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: The excellent, the golden son: where now hast thou aban- doned him?
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96
properties.source_locator: kanda 20, hymn 129, printed label '5', printed as one unit covering verses 5-6

properties.text: There where around those distant trees, three Sisus that are standing there,

properties.source_locator: kanda 20, hymn 129, printed label '7', printed as one unit covering verses 7-8

properties.text: Three adders, breathing angrily, are blowing loud the threatening horn.

properties.source_locator: kanda 20, hymn 129, printed label '9', printed as one unit covering verses 9-10

properties.text: Hither hath come a stallion: he is known by droppings on his way,
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96
properties.source_locator: kanda 20, hymn 129, printed label '11', printed as one unit covering verses 11-12

properties.text: As by their dung the course of kine. What wouldst thou in the home of men?
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96
properties.source_locator: kanda 20, hymn 129, printed label '13', printed as one unit covering verses 13-14

properties.text: Barley and ripened rice I seek. On rice and barley hast thou fed,
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96
properties.source_locator: kanda 20, hymn 129, printed label '15', printed as one unit covering verses 15-16

properties.text: As the big serpent feeds on sheep. Cow's hoof and horse's tail hast thou,
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96
properties.source_locator: kanda 20, hymn 129, printed label '17', printed as one unit covering verses 17-18

properties.text: Winged with a falcon's pinion is that harmless swelling of thy tongue.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96
properties.source_locator: kanda 20, hymn 129, printed label '19', printed as one unit covering verses 19-20

properties.text: Who carried off these stores of milk? Who took the dark cow's milk away?
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: When, O Nāsatyas, we this day make you speed hither N ith our hymns, Or, Asvins, with our songs of praise, remember Kānva specially.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: As erst Kakshivān and the Rishi Vyasva, as erst Dirghatamas invoked your presence, Or, in the sacrificial chambers, Vainya Prithī, so be ye mindful of us here, O Asvins.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Come as home-guardians, saving us from foemen, guarding our living creatures and our bodies, Come to the house to give us seed and offspring:
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Whatever with Indra ye be faring, Asvins, or resting in one dwelling-place with Vāyu, In concord with the Ribhus or Ādityas, or standing still in Vishnu's striding-places.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: When 1, O Asvins, call on you to-day that I may gather strength, Or as all-conquering might in war, be that the Asvins' noblest grace.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Now come, ye Asvins, hitherward: here are oblations set for you; These Soma draughts to aid Yadu and Turvasa, these offered you mid Kanva's sons.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Whatever healing balm is yours, Nāsatyas near or far away, Therewith, great Sages, grant a home to Vatsa and to Vimāda.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Together with the Goddess, with the Asvins' Speech have I awoke. Thou, Goddess, hast disclosed the hymn and holy gift from mortal men.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Awake the Asvins, Goddess Dawn! Up, mighty Lady of Sweet Strains! Rise straightway, priest of sacrifice! High glory to the glad- dening draught!
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Thou, Dawn, approaching with thy light, shinest together with the Sun, And to this man-protecting home the chariot of the Asvins comes.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: When yellow stalks give forth the juice as cows from udders pour their milk, And voices sound the song of praise, the Asvins' worshippers show first.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Forward for glory and for strength, protection that shall con- quer men, And power and skill, most sapient Ones!
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: When, Asvins worthy of our lauds, ye seat you in the father's house. With wisdom or the bliss ye bring.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: We invocate this day your car, far-spreading, O Asvins, even the gathering of the sunlight, Car praised in hymns, most ample, rich in treasure, fitted with seats, the car that beareth Sūryā.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Asvins, ye gained that glory by your Godhead, ye Sons of Heaven, by your own might and power. Food followeth close upon your bright appearing when stately horses in your chariot draw you.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Who bringeth you to-day for help with offered oblations, or with hymns to drink the juices? Who, for the sacrifice's ancient lover, turneth you hither, Asvins, offering homage?
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Borne on your golden car, ye omnipresent! come to this sacrifice of ours, Nāsatyas. Drink of the pleasant liquor of the Soma: give riches to the people who adore you.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Come hitherward to us from earth, from heaven, borne on your golden chariot rolling lightly. Suffer not other worshippers to stay you: here are ye bound by earlier bonds of friendship.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Now for us both, mete out, O Wonder-Workers, riches exceed- ing great with store of heroes, Because the men have sent you praise, O Asvins, and Ajamīlhas come to the laudation.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Whene'er I gratified you here together, your grace was given us, O ye rich in booty. Protect, ye twain, the singer of your praises: to you, Nāsatyas, is my wish directed.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Sweet be the plants for us, the heavens, the waters, and full of sweets for us be air's mid-region! May the Field's Lord for us be full of sweetness, and may we follow after him uninjured.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: Asvins, that work of yours deserves our wonder, the Bull of firmament and earth and heaven; Yes, and your thousand promises in battle. Come near to all these men and drink beside us.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Atharvaveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1895-96

properties.text: WE will present fair praise unto the Mighty One, our hymns to Indra in Vivasvān's dwelling-place; For he hath ne’er found wealth in those who seem to sleep: those who give wealth to men accept no paltry praise.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda, 2nd ed., E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1896

properties.text: HE who gives food, like patrimonial riches and guides aright like some wise man's instruction, Loved like a guest who lies in pleasant lodging,—may he, as Priest, prosper his servant's dwelling.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda, 2nd ed., E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1896

properties.text: 'Through many autumns have I toiled and laboured, at night and morn, through age-inducing dawnings. Old age impairs the beauty of our bodies. Let husbands still come near unto their spouses.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda, 2nd ed., E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1896

properties.text: For even the men aforetime, law-fulfillers, who with the Gods declared eternal statutes,— They have decided, but have not accomplished: so now let Wives come near unto their husbands.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda, 2nd ed., E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1896

properties.text: Non inutilis est labor cui Dii favent: nos omnes aemulos et aemulas vincamus. Superemus in hac centum artium pugna in qua duas partes convenientes utrinque commovemus.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda, 2nd ed., E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1896

properties.language_correction: staged as 'en'; the literal is Griffith's Latin substitution, verified against the pinned source page

properties.text: This Soma I address that is most near us, that which hath been imbibed within the spirit, To pardon any sins we have committed. Verily mortal man is full of longings.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda, 2nd ed., E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1896

properties.text: Agastya thus, toiling with strong endeavour, wishing for children, progeny and power, Cherished—a sage of mighty strength—both classes, and with the Gods obtained his prayer's fulfilment. By 'both classes' probably priests and princes, or institutors of sacrifices, are meant. M. Bergaigne understands the expression to mean the two forms or essences of Soma, the celestial and the terrestrial.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda, 2nd ed., E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1896

properties.text: Membrum suum virile, quod vrotentum fuerat, mas ille retraxit. Rursus illud quod in juvenem filiam sublatum fuerat, non aggressurus, ad se rerahit.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda, 2nd ed., E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1896

properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda, 2nd ed., E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1896

properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda, 2nd ed., E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1896

properties.text:
These waters teem with sacred food: rich in that food, one
longs for them.
Rich be the holy rite therein. In sacred food be Sûrya rich.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Texts of the White Yajurveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1899
properties.source_locator: book page wyvbk06.htm, printed page 48, document unit 22, printed label '23'

properties.text:
Thee for the heart, thee for the mind, thee for the heaven,
thee for the Sun.
Bear up erect to heaven, to Gods, this rite these sacrificial
calls.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Texts of the White Yajurveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1899
properties.source_locator: book page wyvbk06.htm, printed page 48, document unit 24, printed label '23'

properties.text:
May this please Savitar and liberal Dhâtar, Prajâpati the
Treasure-Guard, bright Agni,
Tvashtar, and Vishnu: blessing him with children, grant
store of riches to the Sacrificer.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Texts of the White Yajurveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1899
properties.source_locator: book page wyvbk08.htm, printed page 62, document unit 16, printed label '17'

properties.text:
O restless Purifying Bath, thou glidest onward restlessly.
May I with aid of Gods remove the stain of sin against the
Gods, and wash away with mortals’ help the wrong that
hath been done to men. Preserve me, God, from injury,
from the loud-roaring demon foe. Thou art the fuel of
the Gods.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Texts of the White Yajurveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1899
properties.source_locator: book page wyvbk08.htm, printed page 64, document unit 26, printed label '17'

properties.text:
The Hamsa homed in light, the Vasu in mid-air, the Priest
beside the altar, Guest within the house,
Dweller in noblest place, mid men, in truth, in sky, born
of flood, kine, truth, mountain, he is holy Law. The Great.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Texts of the White Yajurveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1899
properties.source_locator: book page wyvbk12.htm, printed page 102, document unit 13, printed label '14'

properties.text:
Again let the Âdityas, Rudras, Yams, and Brahmans with
their rites light thee, Wealth-bringer!
Increase thy body with presented butter: effectual be the
Sacrificer's wishes.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Texts of the White Yajurveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1899
properties.source_locator: book page wyvbk12.htm, printed page 105, document unit 42, printed label '14'

properties.text:
The keen-shared plough that bringeth bliss, good for the
Soma-drinker's need,
Shear out for me a cow, a sheep, a rapid drawer of the car,
a blooming woman, plump and strong!
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Texts of the White Yajurveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1899
properties.source_locator: book page wyvbk12.htm, printed page 109, document unit 69, printed label '71'

properties.text:
The year together with the darksome fortnights; Dawn with
the ruddy-coloured cows about her; the Asvins with
their wonderful achievements; the Sun together with his
dappled Courser; Vaisvânara with Idâ and with butter.
Svâhâ!
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Texts of the White Yajurveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1899
properties.source_locator: book page wyvbk12.htm, printed page 109, document unit 72, printed label '71'

properties.text:
Homage to the swift, and to the active be homage, and to
the hasty and to the rapid mover be homage! Homage to
him who dwells in waves, and in still waters, to him who
dwells in rivers and on islands.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Texts of the White Yajurveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1899
properties.source_locator: book page wyvbk16.htm, printed page 143, document unit 30, printed label '31'

properties.text:
Homage to him in woods and to him in bushes, homage!
Homage to him as sound and to him as echo, homage!
Homage to him with swift armies and to him with swift
chariots, homage! Homage to the hero, and to him who
rends asunder be homage.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Texts of the White Yajurveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1899
properties.source_locator: book page wyvbk16.htm, printed page 144, document unit 33, printed label '31'

properties.text:
Symbol of milk are barley-grains, symbol of curd are
jujube-fruits.
Whey is the type of Soma, and milk-mixture type of
Soma's pap.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Texts of the White Yajurveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1899
properties.source_locator: book page wyvbk19.htm, printed page 175, document unit 22, printed label '23'

properties.text:
By sacrificial texts are gained the Grahas, and by the Grahas
lauds and laud-arrangements.
By metres are obtained Ukthas and praise-songs, and by the
Sâma-chant the Avabhritha.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Texts of the White Yajurveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1899
properties.source_locator: book page wyvbk19.htm, printed page 176, document unit 27, printed label '23'

properties.text:
All essence of thine own in plants collected, all strength of
Soma when poured out with Surâ—
Therewith impel with joy the sacrifice, Sarasvatî, the Asvins,
Indra, Agni.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Texts of the White Yajurveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1899
properties.source_locator: book page wyvbk19.htm, printed page 177, document unit 32, printed label '33'

properties.text:
Agni, thou poorest life: send down upon us food and vigorous
strength.
Drive thou misfortune far away.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Texts of the White Yajurveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1899
properties.source_locator: book page wyvbk19.htm, printed page 177, document unit 37, printed label '33'

properties.text:
Wealthy in spoil, enriched with hymns, may pure Sarasvatî
desire with eager love our sacrifice.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Texts of the White Yajurveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1899
properties.source_locator: book page wyvbk20.htm, printed page 195, document unit 83, printed label '84'

properties.text:
Sarasvatî, the mighty flood, she with her light illuminates,
she brightens every pious thought.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Texts of the White Yajurveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1899
properties.source_locator: book page wyvbk20.htm, printed page 195, document unit 85, printed label '85'

properties.text:
Let the Hotar worship the Asvins. Let them eat of the
he-goat, the sacrifice. Let them to-day eat the fat, taken
from the middle, before those who hate us, before human
handling. Yea, let them eat amid the fodder of fields
fresh with moisture, with their expanse of barley, limbs
of those tasted by Agni, belonging to the Hundred Rudras,
portions covered with fat, from the sides, from the thighs,
from the fore-feet from the chine. From every member
of the divided victims these two make their repast. Thus
let the Asvins accept. Hotar, offer the sacrificial oblation.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Texts of the White Yajurveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1899
properties.source_locator: book page wyvbk21.htm, printed page 201, document unit 42, printed label '43'

properties.text:
Hail to vital breath! Hail to out-breathing! Hail to
diffusive breath! Hail to the eye! Hail to the ear! Hail
to Speech! Hail to Mind!
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Texts of the White Yajurveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1899
properties.source_locator: book page wyvbk22.htm, printed page 208, document unit 22, printed label '23'

properties.text:
Hail to the lunar asterisms! Hail to those connected with
the lunar asterisms! Hail to Day and Night! Hail to
the half-months! Hail to the mouths! Hail to the Seasons!
Hail to the Season-groups! Hail to the Year!
Hail to Heaven and Earth! Hail to the Moon! Hail to
the Sun! Hail to his rays! Hail to the Vasus! Hail to
the Rudras! Hail to the Âdityas! Hail to the Maruts!
Earl to the All-Gods! Hail to roots! Hail to branches!
Hail to forest trees! Hail to flowers! Hail to fruits!
Hail to herbs!
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Texts of the White Yajurveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1899
properties.source_locator: book page wyvbk22.htm, printed page 209, document unit 27, printed label '23'

properties.text:
Sixfold its form, its syllables a hundred, eighty burnt-offerings,
just three brands for kindling.
To thee I tell the rites of sacrificing. Seven Hotars worship
in appointed season.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Texts of the White Yajurveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1899
properties.source_locator: book page wyvbk23.htm, printed page 216, document unit 45, printed label '68'

properties.text:
Thine is this Soma: come thou near, approach it. Drink
thou thereof, benevolent, and cease not.
Sit on the sacred grass at this our worship, and take these
drops into thy belly, Indra.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Texts of the White Yajurveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1899
properties.source_locator: book page wyvbk26.htm, printed page 234, document unit 22, printed label '28'

properties.text:
Tanûnapât the Asura, all-possessing, God among Gods, the
God with mead and butter shall bedew the paths.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Texts of the White Yajurveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1899
properties.source_locator: book page wyvbk27.htm, printed page 236, document unit 11, printed label '13'

properties.text:
With mead to sacrifice thou comest, Agni, earnest as friendly-
minded Narâsamsa, and Savitar righteous God who brings
all blessings.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Texts of the White Yajurveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1899
properties.source_locator: book page wyvbk27.htm, printed page 236, document unit 12, printed label '13'

properties.text:
What time the mighty waters came containing the universal
germ, producing Agni,
Thence sprang the Gods’ one spirit into being. What God
shall we adore with our oblation?
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Texts of the White Yajurveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1899
properties.source_locator: book page wyvbk27.htm, printed page 237, document unit 24, printed label '26'

properties.text:
Who in his might surveyed the floods enclosing productive
force and generating Worship,
He who is God mid Gods, and none beside him—What God
shall we adore with our oblation?
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Texts of the White Yajurveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1899
properties.source_locator: book page wyvbk27.htm, printed page 237, document unit 25, printed label '26'

properties.text:
The grassy robe of water-plants, divine, hath heightened
Indra's strength.
This, the fair seat where Indra sits, hath topped all other
sacred grass. For gain of wealth let it enjoy. Pay sacrifice.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Texts of the White Yajurveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1899
properties.source_locator: book page wyvbk28.htm, printed page 243, document unit 20, printed label '21'

properties.text:
Let the Priest worship Agni, Indra, kindled, splendidly
kindled, excellent strength-giver,
Lending him mighty power, Gâyatrî metre, a cow aged
eighteen months, and vital vigour. Let him enjoy the
butter. Hotar, worship.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Texts of the White Yajurveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1899
properties.source_locator: book page wyvbk28.htm, printed page 243, document unit 23, printed label '21'

properties.text:
Symmetrical in flank, with rounded haunches, mettled like
heroes, the celestial Coursers
Put forth their strength like swans in lengthened order when
they, the Steeds, have reached the heavenly causeway.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Texts of the White Yajurveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1899
properties.source_locator: book page wyvbk29.htm, printed page 249, document unit 20, printed label '21'

properties.text:
The Steed is come unto the noblest mansion, is come unto
his Father and his Mother.
This day shall he approach the Gods, most welcome: then
he declares good gifts to him who worships.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Texts of the White Yajurveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1899
properties.source_locator: book page wyvbk29.htm, printed page 250, document unit 23, printed label '21'

properties.text:
He lays his blows upon their backs, He deals his strokes
upon their thighs.
Thou Whip who urgest horses, drive sagacious chargers in
the fray.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Texts of the White Yajurveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1899
properties.source_locator: book page wyvbk29.htm, printed page 253, document unit 49, printed label '59'

properties.text:
To Agni Anîkavân is sacrificed a red-marked ox; two with
white spots below are for Savitar; two with silvery navels
for Pûshan; two yellow hornless he-goats for the All-Gods;
a spotted one for the Maruts; the black-faced he-goat is
Agni's; the ewe is Sarasvatî's; the ram is Varuna's.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Texts of the White Yajurveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1899
properties.source_locator: book page wyvbk29.htm, printed page 254, document unit 58, printed label '59'

properties.text:
In the sky's lap the Sun this form assumeth that Varuna
and Mitra may behold it.
His Bay Steeds well maintain their power eternal, at one
time bright, and darksome at another.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Texts of the White Yajurveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1899
properties.source_locator: book page wyvbk33.htm, printed page 272, document unit 36, printed label '38'

properties.text:
Approach ye, and be near to us. Drink, O ye Asvins, of
the mead.
Draw forth the milk, ye mighty, rich in genuine wealth!
Injure us not, and come to us.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Texts of the White Yajurveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1899
properties.source_locator: book page wyvbk33.htm, printed page 278, document unit 86, printed label '38'

properties.text:
Worthy to be revered, O Agni, God, preserve our wealthy
patrons with thy succours, and ourselves.
Guard art thou of our seed and progeny and cows, incessantly
protecting in thy holy law.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Texts of the White Yajurveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1899
properties.source_locator: book page wyvbk34.htm, printed page 281, document unit 12, printed label '15'

properties.text:
In Idâ's place, the centre of the earth, will we deposit thee,
That, Agni Jâtavedas, thou mayst bear our offerings to the
Gods.
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Texts of the White Yajurveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1899
properties.source_locator: book page wyvbk34.htm, printed page 281, document unit 14, printed label '15'

properties.text:
Homage to thee the lightning flash, homage to thee the
thunder's roar!
Homage, O Bounteous Lord, to thee whereas thou fain
wouldst win to heaven!
properties.work_edition: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Texts of the White Yajurveda, E. J. Lazarus, Benares, 1899
properties.source_locator: book page wyvbk36.htm, printed page 292, document unit 19, printed label '21'
